No implementation details, audio interface description, or silicon test results are provided.

The only external hardware named is the TinyVGA PMOD, and the design is a single 1x1 tile implemented in Verilog. results.summary_before: This is a parity detector that turns on an LED when an even number of its eight switch inputs are high, and turns it off for an odd number. It is built from six XOR gates and is tested by toggling the input switches and observing the parity output. No external hardware beyond the switches and LED is required. The documentation is very brief and does not include a schematic or detailed explanation.
results.summary: This is a parity detector that controls an LED output based on the number of active switch inputs. The documentation describes it as turning off the parity LED when an odd number of switches are on, built from six XOR gates, and tested by toggling the switches. No external hardware beyond the switches and LED is required. The documentation is very brief and does not include a schematic or detailed explanation.

results.summary_before: This design provides control logic for test pads on the north side of the TTGF0p1 die, allowing configuration bits to be set and read back. It uses a config bit index and toggle signals to select and modify configuration bits, with outputs reflecting pad inputs and the selected config bit value. The design is intended for silicon testing and does not require external hardware beyond the chip's pads. The documentation is sparse and focuses on pin functions rather than a full description.

results.summary_before: This is an analog bandgap voltage reference based on a Beta amplifier topology with a folded cascode OTA. It provides a typical output voltage of approximately 1.23 V. The circuit includes a buffer for one output node and requires an external DC voltage source for testing. Silicon measurements showed a Vref of 1.26 V, close to the expected value.
